sentences.zh: 于休烈

translations.literal: Yu Xiulie
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xiulie

sentences.zh: 于休烈，河南人也。

translations.literal: Yu Xiulie was a native of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xiulie came from Henan.

sentences.zh: 高祖志寧，貞觀中任左僕射，為十八學士。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zhining served as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs in the Zhenguan era and was one of the Eighteen Scholars.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zhining had served as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs under Zhenguan and was numbered among the Eighteen Scholars.

sentences.zh: 父默成，沛縣令，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Mocheng was magistrate of Pei County and died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mocheng had been magistrate of Pei County and died young.

sentences.zh: 休烈至性貞愨，機鑒敏悟。

translations.literal: Xiulie was upright by nature and keenly perceptive.
translations.idiomatic: Xiulie was upright by nature, with a sharp and discerning mind.

sentences.zh: 自幼好學，善屬文，與會稽賀朝、萬齊融、延陵包融為文詞之友，齊名一時。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning and was skilled at composition; with He Chao of Kuaiji, Wan Qirong, and Bao Rong of Yanling he formed a circle of literary friends and was famed together for a time.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he loved study and wrote well. With He Chao of Kuaiji, Wan Qirong, and Bao Rong of Yanling he formed a circle of literary friends, and for a time their names were linked together.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，又應制策登科，授秘書省正字。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, also passed the decree examination, and was appointed proofreader in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and also placed on the decree examination, then was appointed a proofreader in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 累遷右補闕、起居郎、集賢殿學士，轉比部員外郎，郎中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Right Remonstrator, Diarist, and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, then transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue and then Director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Right Remonstrator, Diarist, and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, then served as Vice Director and then Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠輔政，排不附己者，出為中部郡太守。

translations.literal: When Yang Guozhong held power, he removed those who would not follow him and sent Xiulie out as prefect of Zhongbu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Guozhong dominated the government, he pushed aside those who would not follow him and sent Xiulie out as prefect of Zhongbu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 值祿山構難，肅宗踐祚，休烈自中部赴行在，擢拜給事中。

translations.literal: When Lushan raised rebellion and Suzong ascended the throne, Xiulie came from Zhongbu to the imperial camp and was promoted to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled and Suzong took the throne, Xiulie came from Zhongbu to the imperial camp and was promoted to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 遷太常少卿，知禮儀事，兼修國史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, put in charge of ritual affairs, and concurrently charged with compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, placed in charge of ritual affairs, and concurrently assigned to compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 肅宗自鳳翔還京，勵精聽受，嘗謂休烈曰：「君舉必書，良史也。

translations.literal: When Suzong returned from Fengxiang to the capital, he applied himself diligently to governance and once said to Xiulie, "You record every action— you are a fine historian.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong returned from Fengxiang to the capital, he applied himself diligently to governance and once said to Xiulie, "You record every action— you are a fine historian.

sentences.zh: 朕有過失，卿書之否？」

translations.literal: If I have faults, will you record them as well?"
translations.idiomatic: If I commit faults, will you write them down too?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「禹、湯罪己，其興也勃焉。

translations.literal: He replied, "Yu and Tang blamed themselves, and their rise was swift.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Yu and Tang blamed themselves, and their rise was swift.

sentences.zh: 有德之君，不忘規過，臣不勝大慶。」

translations.literal: A ruler of virtue does not forget to be corrected; your subject cannot contain his great joy."
translations.idiomatic: A ruler of virtue never forgets to be corrected. Your subject is filled with joy at this."

sentences.zh: 時中原蕩覆，典章殆盡，無史籍檢尋。

translations.literal: At that time the Central Plain was overturned and canonical institutions were nearly lost; there were no historical records to consult.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Central Plain lay in ruins and canonical institutions were nearly lost; there were no historical records to consult.

sentences.zh: 休烈奏曰：「《國史》一百六卷，《開元實錄》四十七卷，起居註並餘書三千六百八十二卷，並在興慶宮史館。

translations.literal: Xiulie memorialized, "The National History in one hundred six juan, the Veritable Record of the Kaiyuan Reign in forty-seven juan, the Diaries of Activity and Rest, and other books totaling three thousand six hundred eighty-two juan are all in the Historiography Office of the Xingqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Xiulie memorialized, "The National History in one hundred six juan, the Veritable Record of the Kaiyuan Reign in forty-seven juan, the Diaries of Activity and Rest, and other books totaling three thousand six hundred eighty-two juan are all in the Historiography Office of the Xingqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 京城陷賊後，皆被焚燒。

translations.literal: After the capital fell to the rebels, all were burned.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital fell to the rebels, all were burned.

sentences.zh: 且《國史》、《實錄》，聖朝大典，修撰多時，今並無本。

translations.literal: Moreover the National History and Veritable Records are great canonical works of the sacred dynasty, compiled over many years, and now there are no originals at all.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the National History and Veritable Records are great canonical works of the sacred dynasty, compiled over many years, and now there are no originals at all.

sentences.zh: 伏望下御史臺推勘史館所由，令府縣招訪。

translations.literal: I respectfully ask that the Censorate be ordered to investigate those responsible in the Historiography Office and have prefectures and counties seek them out.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully ask that the Censorate investigate those responsible in the Historiography Office and have prefectures and counties seek the books out.

sentences.zh: 有人別收得《國史》、《實錄》，如送官司，重加購賞。

translations.literal: If anyone has separately recovered the National History or Veritable Records and delivers them to the authorities, let a heavy reward be added.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone has separately recovered the National History or Veritable Records and delivers them to the authorities, let a heavy reward be added.

sentences.zh: 若是史官收得，仍赦其罪。

translations.literal: If a historiographer recovered them, still pardon his offense.
translations.idiomatic: If a historiographer recovered them, still pardon his offense.

sentences.zh: 得一部，超授官資，得一卷賞絹十匹。」

translations.literal: For recovering one complete work, grant an extraordinary promotion; for one juan, reward ten bolts of silk."
translations.idiomatic: For recovering one complete work, grant an extraordinary promotion; for one juan, reward ten bolts of silk."

sentences.zh: 數月之內，唯得一兩卷。

translations.literal: Within a few months only one or two juan were recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months only one or two juan were recovered.

sentences.zh: 前修史官工部侍郎韋述陷賊，入東京，至是以其家藏《國史》一百一十三卷送於官。

translations.literal: The former historiographer and Vice Director of the Ministry of Works Wei Shu, who had fallen into rebel hands and entered the Eastern Capital, at this time sent the National History in one hundred thirteen juan from his family collection to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: The former historiographer and Vice Director of the Ministry of Works Wei Shu, who had fallen into rebel hands and entered the Eastern Capital, at this time sent the National History in one hundred thirteen juan from his family collection to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 肅宗以太常鐘磬，自隋已來，所傳五音，或有不調，乾元初謂休烈曰：「古者聖人作樂，以應天地之和，以合陰陽之序，則人不夭紮，物不疵癘。

translations.literal: Suzong, regarding the bells and chimes of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, held that since Sui times the five tones handed down had at times been out of tune; at the beginning of the Qianyuan era he said to Xiulie, "In antiquity the sages made music to accord with the harmony of Heaven and earth and to fit the order of yin and yang, so that people did not die young and things were not afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong, regarding the bells and chimes of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, held that since Sui times the five tones handed down had at times been out of tune; at the beginning of the Qianyuan era he said to Xiulie, "In antiquity the sages made music to accord with the harmony of Heaven and earth and to fit the order of yin and yang, so that people did not die young and things were not afflicted.

sentences.zh: 且金石絲竹，樂之器也。

translations.literal: Metal, stone, silk, and bamboo are the instruments of music.
translations.idiomatic: Metal, stone, silk, and bamboo are the instruments of music.

sentences.zh: 比親享郊廟，每聽懸樂，宮商不備，或鐘磬失度。

translations.literal: Recently, whenever I personally performed the suburban and ancestral sacrifices and listened to the suspended music, the pitch modes were incomplete or the bells and chimes were off pitch.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, whenever I personally performed the suburban and ancestral sacrifices and listened to the suspended music, the pitch modes were incomplete or the bells and chimes were off pitch.

sentences.zh: 可盡將鐘磬來，朕當於內自定。」

translations.literal: Bring all the bells and chimes here; I shall set the pitch myself within the palace."
translations.idiomatic: Bring all the bells and chimes here; I shall set the pitch myself within the palace."

sentences.zh: 太常集樂工考試，數日審知差錯，然後令別鑄造磨刻。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices assembled music masters to test them; after several days the errors were identified, and then new casting, carving, and polishing were ordered.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices assembled music masters to test them; after several days the errors were identified, and then new casting, carving, and polishing were ordered.

sentences.zh: 及事畢，上臨殿親試考擊，皆合五音，群臣稱慶。

translations.literal: When the work was finished, the emperor personally tested them in the hall; all matched the five tones, and the officials congratulated him.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, the emperor personally tested them in the hall; all matched the five tones, and the officials congratulated him.

sentences.zh: 休烈尋轉工部侍郎、修國史，獻《五代帝王論》，帝甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Xiulie was soon transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and compiler of the national history; he presented An Essay on the Five Dynasties' Emperors, and the emperor greatly praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiulie was soon transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and compiler of the national history; he presented An Essay on the Five Dynasties' Emperors, and the emperor greatly praised it.

sentences.zh: 宰相李揆矜能忌賢，以休烈修國史與己齊列，嫉之，奏為國子祭酒，權留史館修撰以下之。

translations.literal: The chancellor Li Kuo, proud of his talent and jealous of the worthy, resented that Xiulie compiled the national history on equal footing with himself; he memorialized to make Xiulie Director of the Directorate of Education while retaining him in the Historiography Office to compile, thereby demoting him.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor Li Kuo, proud of his talent and jealous of the worthy, resented that Xiulie compiled the national history on equal footing with himself; he memorialized to make Xiulie Director of the Directorate of Education while retaining him in the Historiography Office to compile, thereby demoting him.

sentences.zh: 休烈恬然自持，殊不介意。

translations.literal: Xiulie remained calm and self-possessed and did not mind at all.
translations.idiomatic: Xiulie remained calm and self-possessed and did not mind at all.

sentences.zh: 舊儀，元正冬至，百官不於光順門朝賀皇后，乾元元年，張皇后遂行此禮。

translations.literal: By old practice, on New Year's Day and the winter solstice officials did not attend court at Guangshun Gate to congratulate the empress; in the first year of Qianyuan, Empress Zhang carried out this rite.
translations.idiomatic: By old practice, on New Year's Day and the winter solstice officials did not attend court at Guangshun Gate to congratulate the empress; in the first year of Qianyuan, Empress Zhang carried out this rite.

sentences.zh: 休烈奏曰：「《周禮》有命夫朝人主，命婦朝女君。

translations.literal: Xiulie memorialized, "The Rites of Zhou provide that titled husbands attend the ruler and titled wives attend the lady.
translations.idiomatic: Xiulie memorialized, "The Rites of Zhou provide that titled husbands attend the ruler and titled wives attend the lady.

sentences.zh: 自顯慶已來，則天皇后始行此禮。

translations.literal: Since the Xianqing era, Empress Wu began this practice.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Xianqing era, Empress Wu began this practice.

sentences.zh: 其日，命婦又朝光順門，與百官雜處，殊為失禮。」

translations.literal: On that day titled wives also attended at Guangshun Gate and mingled with officials— a grave breach of ritual."
translations.idiomatic: On that day titled wives also attended at Guangshun Gate and mingled with officials— a grave breach of ritual."

sentences.zh: 肅宗詔停之。

translations.literal: Suzong issued an edict stopping it.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong issued an edict stopping it.

sentences.zh: 代宗即位，甄別名品，宰臣元載稱之，乃拜右散騎常侍，依前兼修國史，尋加禮儀使。

translations.literal: When Daizong ascended the throne and ranked officials by quality, the chancellor Yuan Zai praised Xiulie; he was appointed Right Regular Attendant and continued to compile the national history, then added Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong ascended the throne and ranked officials by quality, the chancellor Yuan Zai praised Xiulie; he was appointed Right Regular Attendant and continued to compile the national history, then added Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 又改檢校工部尚書，兼判太常卿事，正拜工部尚書，累封東海郡公，加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was then changed to Acting Director of the Ministry of Works and concurrently judged affairs of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, formally appointed Director of the Ministry of Works, enfeoffed as Duke of Donghai Commandery, and granted the Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He was then changed to Acting Director of the Ministry of Works and concurrently judged affairs of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, formally appointed Director of the Ministry of Works, enfeoffed as Duke of Donghai Commandery, and granted the Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 在朝凡三十餘年，歷掌清要，家無提石之蓄。

translations.literal: In court for more than thirty years, he repeatedly held prestigious posts, yet his household had no store of even a few pecks of grain.
translations.idiomatic: In court for more than thirty years, he repeatedly held prestigious posts, yet his household had no store of even a few pecks of grain.

sentences.zh: 恭儉溫仁，未嘗以喜慍形於顏色。

translations.literal: Respectful, frugal, and gentle, he never showed joy or anger in his face.
translations.idiomatic: Respectful, frugal, and gentle, he never showed joy or anger in his face.

sentences.zh: 而親賢下士，推轂後進，雖位崇年高，曾無倦色。

translations.literal: Yet he honored the worthy and treated inferiors well, promoting later generations; though high in rank and advanced in years, he never showed weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he honored the worthy and treated inferiors well, promoting later generations; though high in rank and advanced in years, he never showed weariness.

sentences.zh: 篤好墳籍，手不釋卷，以至於終。

translations.literal: He deeply loved the classics and never put books down, even to the end.
translations.idiomatic: He deeply loved the classics and never put books down, even to the end.

sentences.zh: 大歷七年卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dali he died at age eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Dali he died at age eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷行於代。

translations.literal: A collection in ten juan circulated in his age.
translations.idiomatic: A collection in ten juan circulated in his age.

sentences.zh: 嗣子益，次子肅，相繼為翰林學士。

translations.literal: His heir Yi and second son Su both served in succession as Hanlin Academicians.
translations.idiomatic: His heir Yi and second son Su both served in succession as Hanlin Academicians.

sentences.zh: 是歲春，休烈妻韋氏卒。

translations.literal: That spring Xiulie's wife, Lady Wei, died.
translations.idiomatic: That spring Xiulie's wife, Lady Wei, died.

sentences.zh: 上以休烈父子儒行著聞，特詔贈韋氏國夫人，葬日給鹵簿鼓吹。

translations.literal: Because the emperor considered the Confucian conduct of Xiulie and his sons renowned, he specially ordered Lady Wei enfeoffed as Lady of the State, and on the day of burial granted an honor guard and musical escort.
translations.idiomatic: Because the emperor considered the Confucian conduct of Xiulie and his sons renowned, he specially ordered Lady Wei enfeoffed as Lady of the State, and on the day of burial granted an honor guard and musical escort.

sentences.zh: 及聞休烈卒，追悼久之，褒贈尚書左僕射，賻絹百匹、布五十端，遣謁者內常侍吳承倩就私第宣慰。

translations.literal: When he heard Xiulie had died, he mourned him for a long time, posthumously granted him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, gave one hundred bolts of silk and fifty bolts of cloth as funeral gifts, and sent Palace Usher and Inner Attendant Wu Chengqian to his private residence to convey consolation.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Xiulie had died, he mourned him for a long time, posthumously granted him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, gave one hundred bolts of silk and fifty bolts of cloth as funeral gifts, and sent Palace Usher and Inner Attendant Wu Chengqian to his private residence to convey consolation.

sentences.zh: 儒者之榮，少有其比。

translations.literal: Few Confucians had such honor.
translations.idiomatic: Few Confucians had such honor.

sentences.zh: 肅官至給事中。

translations.literal: Su rose to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Su rose to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 肅子敖。

translations.literal: Su's son Ao.
translations.idiomatic: Su's son Ao.

sentences.zh: 敖字蹈中，以家世文史盛名。

translations.literal: Ao, styled Daozhong, was famed for his family's literary and historical tradition.
translations.idiomatic: Ao, styled Daozhong, was famed for his family's literary and historical tradition.

sentences.zh: 少為時彥所稱，誌行修謹。

translations.literal: In youth he was praised by men of the age for his conduct and was careful in word and deed.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was praised by men of the age for his conduct and was careful in word and deed.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，釋褐秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and on leaving office was appointed collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and on leaving office was appointed collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 湖南觀察使楊憑辟為從事；

translations.literal: The Hunan Observation Commissioner Yang Ping recruited him as aide;
translations.idiomatic: The Hunan Observation Commissioner Yang Ping recruited him as aide;

sentences.zh: 府罷，鳳翔節度使李鄘、鄂嶽觀察使呂元膺相繼辟召。

translations.literal: when that office closed, the Fengxiang Military Commissioner Li Yong and the E-Yue Observation Commissioner Lü Yuanying recruited him in succession.
translations.idiomatic: when that office closed, the Fengxiang Military Commissioner Li Yong and the E-Yue Observation Commissioner Lü Yuanying recruited him in succession.

sentences.zh: 自協律郎、大理評事試監察御史，元和六年，真拜監察御史，轉殿中，歷倉部司勛二員外、萬年令，拜右司郎中，出為商州刺史。

translations.literal: From Director of Music, Grand Court Assessor, and Acting Investigating Censor, in the sixth year of Yuanhe he was formally appointed Investigating Censor, transferred to the Palace Secretariat, served as Vice Director in the Granaries and Merits ministries, magistrate of Wannian County, appointed Right Director in the Secretariat, and went out as prefect of Shang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: From Director of Music, Grand Court Assessor, and Acting Investigating Censor, in the sixth year of Yuanhe he was formally appointed Investigating Censor, transferred to the Palace Secretariat, served as Vice Director in the Granaries and Merits ministries, magistrate of Wannian County, appointed Right Director in the Secretariat, and went out as prefect of Shang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 長慶四年，入為吏部郎中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Changqing he entered court as Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Changqing he entered court as Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 其年，遷給事中。

translations.literal: That year he was transferred to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was transferred to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 昭湣初即位，李逢吉用事，與翰林學士李紳素不葉，遂誣紳以不測之罪，逐於嶺外。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong of Zhaomin first ascended the throne, Li Fengji held power; he and Hanlin Academician Li Shen had long been at odds, so he falsely charged Shen with an unforeseeable crime and banished him beyond the Ling mountain range.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong of Zhaomin first ascended the throne, Li Fengji held power; he and Hanlin Academician Li Shen had long been at odds, so he falsely charged Shen with an unforeseeable crime and banished him beyond the Ling mountain range.

sentences.zh: 紳同職駕部郎中知制誥龐嚴、司封員外郎知制誥蔣防，坐紳黨左遷信、汀等州刺史。

translations.literal: Shen's colleagues, Drafting Director of the Transport Bureau and Drafter of Edicts Pang Yan, and Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites and Drafter of Edicts Jiang Fang, were demoted as Shen's faction to prefects of Xin, Ting, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's colleagues, Drafting Director of the Transport Bureau and Drafter of Edicts Pang Yan, and Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites and Drafter of Edicts Jiang Fang, were demoted as Shen's faction to prefects of Xin, Ting, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 黜詔下，敖封還詔書。

translations.literal: When the demotion edict was issued, Ao sealed and returned the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When the demotion edict was issued, Ao sealed and returned the edict.

sentences.zh: 時人以為與嚴相善，訴其非罪，皆曰：「於給事犯宰執之怒，伸龐、蔣之屈，不亦仁乎？」

translations.literal: People at the time thought he was on good terms with Yan and were protesting their innocence, all saying, "Supervising Censor Yu has offended the chief minister yet speaks up for Pang and Jiang's wrong— is that not humane?"
translations.idiomatic: People at the time thought he was on good terms with Yan and were protesting their innocence, all saying, "Supervising Censor Yu has offended the chief minister yet speaks up for Pang and Jiang's wrong— is that not humane?"

sentences.zh: 及駁奏出，乃是論龐嚴貶黜太輕，中外無不大噱，而逢吉由是獎之。

translations.literal: When the rebuttal memorial came out, it in fact argued that Pang Yan's demotion was too light; inside and outside the court there was great ridicule, yet Fengji therefore rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebuttal memorial came out, it in fact argued that Pang Yan's demotion was too light; inside and outside the court there was great ridicule, yet Fengji therefore rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 尋轉工部侍郎，遷刑部，出為宣歙觀察使、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, then Minister of Justice, and went out as Observation Commissioner of Xuan and She and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, then Minister of Justice, and went out as Observation Commissioner of Xuan and She and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 敖溫裕長者，與物無忤，居官亦未嘗有立。

translations.literal: Ao was mild and long-suffering and got along with no one; in office he never took a stand.
translations.idiomatic: Ao was mild and long-suffering and got along with no one; in office he never took a stand.

sentences.zh: 周踐臺閣，三為列曹侍郎，謹順自容而已。

translations.literal: For years he passed through the central offices and three times served as Vice Director of a ministry, merely keeping himself unobtrusive.
translations.idiomatic: For years he passed through the central offices and three times served as Vice Director of a ministry, merely keeping himself unobtrusive.

sentences.zh: 太和四年八月卒，年六十六，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Taihe he died at age sixty-six and was posthumously granted Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Taihe he died at age sixty-six and was posthumously granted Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 四子：球、珪、瑰、琮，皆登進士第。

translations.literal: Four sons: Qiu, Gui, Gui, and Cong— all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Four sons: Qiu, Gui, Gui, and Cong— all passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 琮，落拓有大志，雖以門資為吏，久不見用。

translations.literal: Cong was unrestrained and had great ambition; though he entered office through family standing, for a long time he was not employed.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was unrestrained and had great ambition; though he entered office through family standing, for a long time he was not employed.

sentences.zh: 大中朝，駙馬都尉鄭顥以琮世故，獨以器度奇之。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong era, the Emperor's Son-in-law Commandant Zheng Hao, because of Cong's family background, alone regarded his capacity as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dazhong era, the Emperor's Son-in-law Commandant Zheng Hao, because of Cong's family background, alone regarded his capacity as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 會有詔於士族中選人才尚公主，衣冠多避之。

translations.literal: When there was an edict to select talent from the gentry to marry a princess, many in official dress avoided it.
translations.idiomatic: When there was an edict to select talent from the gentry to marry a princess, many in official dress avoided it.

sentences.zh: 顥謂琮曰：「子人才甚佳，但不護細行，為世譽所抑，久而不調，能應此命乎？」

translations.literal: Hao said to Cong, "Your talent is excellent, but you do not guard small conduct and are suppressed by public reputation; long without promotion— can you answer this appointment?"
translations.idiomatic: Hao said to Cong, "Your talent is excellent, but you do not guard small conduct and are suppressed by public reputation; long without promotion— can you answer this appointment?"

sentences.zh: 琮然之。

translations.literal: Cong agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Cong agreed.

sentences.zh: 會李籓知貢舉，顥托之登第；

translations.literal: When Li Fan supervised the examination, Hao secured his passing;
translations.idiomatic: When Li Fan supervised the examination, Hao secured his passing;

sentences.zh: 其年遂升諫列，尚廣德公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: that year he rose to the remonstrance ranks, married Princess Guangde, and was appointed Emperor's Son-in-law Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: that year he rose to the remonstrance ranks, married Princess Guangde, and was appointed Emperor's Son-in-law Commandant.

sentences.zh: 累踐臺閣，揚歷籓府。

translations.literal: He repeatedly passed through the central offices and served in succession in provincial administrations.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly passed through the central offices and served in succession in provincial administrations.

sentences.zh: 乾符中同平章事。

translations.literal: In the Qianfu era he served as Co-Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianfu era he served as Co-Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 黃寇犯京師，僖宗出幸，琮病不能從。

translations.literal: When the Yellow Bandits invaded the capital and Emperor Xizong fled, Cong was ill and could not follow.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow Bandits invaded the capital and Emperor Xizong fled, Cong was ill and could not follow.

sentences.zh: 既僭號，起琮為相。

translations.literal: After they usurped the title, they raised Cong as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: After they usurped the title, they raised Cong as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 琮以疾辭。

translations.literal: Cong declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Cong declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 迫脅不已，琮曰：「吾病亟矣，死在旦夕。

translations.literal: When coercion did not cease, Cong said, "My illness is grave and death is near at hand.
translations.idiomatic: When coercion did not cease, Cong said, "My illness is grave and death is near at hand.

sentences.zh: 加以唐室親姻，義不受命，死即甘心。」

translations.literal: Moreover, as kin of the Tang house, by principle I cannot accept the appointment; if I die, I accept it willingly."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as kin of the Tang house, by principle I cannot accept the appointment; if I die, I accept it willingly."

sentences.zh: 竟為賊所害，而赦公主。

translations.literal: In the end he was killed by the bandits, and the princess was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was killed by the bandits, and the princess was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 主視琮受禍，謂賊曰：「妾李氏女也，義不獨存，願與於公並命。」

translations.literal: Seeing Cong suffer calamity, the princess said to the bandits, "I am a daughter of the Li house; by principle I cannot live alone. I wish to die together with Lord Yu."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Cong suffer calamity, the princess said to the bandits, "I am a daughter of the Li house; by principle I cannot live alone. I wish to die together with Lord Yu."

sentences.zh: 賊不許，公主入室自縊而卒。

translations.literal: The bandits would not allow it; the princess entered her chamber and hanged herself to death.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits would not allow it; the princess entered her chamber and hanged herself to death.

sentences.zh: 廣德閨門有禮，咸通、乾符中譽在人口。

translations.literal: Princess Guangde's household observed ritual propriety; in the Xian Tong and Qianfu eras her reputation was on everyone's lips.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Guangde's household observed ritual propriety; in the Xian Tong and Qianfu eras her reputation was on everyone's lips.

sentences.zh: 於族內外冠婚喪祭，主必自預行禮，諸婦班而見之，尊卑答勞，鹹有儀法，為時所稱。

translations.literal: Within and outside the clan at weddings, funerals, and sacrifices, the princess always attended in person to perform the rites; the wives lined up to see her, and superiors and inferiors exchanged courtesies and labor— all with proper forms, and she was praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Within and outside the clan at weddings, funerals, and sacrifices, the princess always attended in person to perform the rites; the wives lined up to see her, and superiors and inferiors exchanged courtesies and labor— all with proper forms, and she was praised by the age.

sentences.zh: 珪、球皆至清顯。

translations.literal: Gui and Qiu both reached clear and prominent rank.
translations.idiomatic: Gui and Qiu both reached clear and prominent rank.

sentences.zh: 令狐峘

translations.literal: Ling Huhuan
translations.idiomatic: Ling Huhuan

sentences.zh: 令狐峘，德棻之玄孫。

translations.literal: Ling Huhuan was a great-great-grandson of Defen.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Huhuan was a great-great-grandson of Defen.

sentences.zh: 登進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，隱居南山豹林谷，谷中有亙別墅。

translations.literal: In the chaos of Lushan's rebellion he hid in Leopard Forest Valley in the Southern Mountains; in the valley was the Gen villa.
translations.idiomatic: In the chaos of Lushan's rebellion he hid in Leopard Forest Valley in the Southern Mountains; in the valley was the Gen villa.

sentences.zh: 司徒楊綰未仕時，避亂南山，止於峘舍。

translations.literal: Minister Yang Wan, before he took office, fled the chaos to the Southern Mountains and stayed at Huhuan's lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Yang Wan, before he took office, fled the chaos to the Southern Mountains and stayed at Huhuan's lodge.

sentences.zh: 峘博學，貫通群書，有口辯，綰甚稱之。

translations.literal: Huhuan was broadly learned, mastered all books, and was eloquent; Wan greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Huhuan was broadly learned, mastered all books, and was eloquent; Wan greatly praised him.

sentences.zh: 及綰為禮部侍郎，修國史，乃引峘入史館。

translations.literal: When Wan became Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and compiled the national history, he brought Huhuan into the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Wan became Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and compiled the national history, he brought Huhuan into the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 自華原尉拜右拾遺，累遷起居舍人，皆兼史職，修《玄宗實錄》一百卷、《代宗實錄》四十卷。

translations.literal: From Magistrate of Huayuan he was appointed Right Remonstrator, repeatedly promoted to Diarist, all concurrently historiographical posts, compiling the Veritable Record of Emperor Xuanzong in one hundred juan and the Veritable Record of Emperor Daizong in forty juan.
translations.idiomatic: From Magistrate of Huayuan he was appointed Right Remonstrator, repeatedly promoted to Diarist, all concurrently historiographical posts, compiling the Veritable Record of Emperor Xuanzong in one hundred juan and the Veritable Record of Emperor Daizong in forty juan.

sentences.zh: 著述雖勤，屬大亂之後，起居註亡失，峘纂開元、天寶事，雖得諸家文集，編其詔策，名臣傳記十無三四，後人以漏落處多，不稱良史。

translations.literal: Though he wrote diligently, it fell after great chaos when the Diaries of Activity and Rest were lost; Huhuan compiled Kaiyuan and Tianbao events and, though he obtained collected works of various houses and edited their edicts and policies, biographies of eminent ministers were three or four in ten; later men, because of many omissions, did not call him a fine historian.
translations.idiomatic: Though he wrote diligently, it fell after great chaos when the Diaries of Activity and Rest were lost; Huhuan compiled Kaiyuan and Tianbao events and, though he obtained collected works of various houses and edited their edicts and policies, biographies of eminent ministers were three or four in ten; later men, because of many omissions, did not call him a fine historian.

sentences.zh: 大歷八年，改刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dali he was changed to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Dali he was changed to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，將厚奉元陵，峘上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: When Dezong ascended the throne and was about to lavishly supply Yuanling, Huhuan submitted a remonstrance memorial:
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong ascended the throne and was about to lavishly supply Yuanling, Huhuan submitted a remonstrance memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞《傳》曰：「近臣盡規」，《禮記》曰：「事君有犯而無隱」。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard the Commentary says, "Close ministers fully remonstrate," and the Book of Rites says, "In serving the ruler there is offense but no concealment."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard the Commentary says, "Close ministers fully remonstrate," and the Book of Rites says, "In serving the ruler there is offense but no concealment."

sentences.zh: 臣幸偶昌運，謬參近列，敢竭狂愚，庶裨分寸，伏惟陛下詳察。

translations.literal: Your subject has fortunately met a prosperous age and wrongly holds a close post; I dare exhaust my rash foolishness, hoping it may help in the least; I respectfully ask Your Majesty to examine it closely.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has fortunately met a prosperous age and wrongly holds a close post; I dare exhaust my rash foolishness, hoping it may help in the least; I respectfully ask Your Majesty to examine it closely.

sentences.zh: 臣讀《漢書·劉向傳》，見論王者山陵之誡，良史稱嘆，萬古芬芳。

translations.literal: Your subject read the Han Annals biography of Liu Xiang and saw the discussion of warnings regarding imperial tombs; fine historians praised it and its fragrance lasts through ten thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject read the Han Annals biography of Liu Xiang and saw the discussion of warnings regarding imperial tombs; fine historians praised it and its fragrance lasts through ten thousand ages.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 聖賢之心，勤儉是務，必求諸道，不作無益。

translations.literal: The minds of sages and worthies take frugality as their task and surely seek the Way, making nothing without benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The minds of sages and worthies take frugality as their task and surely seek the Way, making nothing without benefit.

sentences.zh: 故舜葬蒼梧，不變其肆；

translations.literal: Therefore Shun was buried at Cangwu without changing its marketplace;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Shun was buried at Cangwu without changing its marketplace;

sentences.zh: 禹葬會稽，不改其列。

translations.literal: Yu was buried at Kuaiji without changing its rows.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was buried at Kuaiji without changing its rows.

sentences.zh: 周武葬於畢陌，無丘壟之處；

translations.literal: King Wu of Zhou was buried at Bimo with no mound or tomb;
translations.idiomatic: King Wu of Zhou was buried at Bimo with no mound or tomb;

sentences.zh: 漢文葬於霸陵，因山谷之勢。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han was buried at Baling following the terrain of valley and hill.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han was buried at Baling following the terrain of valley and hill.

sentences.zh: 禹非不忠也，啟非不順也，周公非不悌也，景帝非不孝也，其奉君親，皆從微薄。

translations.literal: Yu was not disloyal, Qi was not unfilial, the Duke of Zhou was not undutiful to younger brothers, and Emperor Jing was not unfilial; in serving ruler and parent they all followed modest practice.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was not disloyal, Qi was not unfilial, the Duke of Zhou was not undutiful to younger brothers, and Emperor Jing was not unfilial; in serving ruler and parent they all followed modest practice.

sentences.zh: 昔宋文公始為厚葬，用蜃炭，益車馬，其臣華元、樂舉，《春秋》書為不臣。

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Wen of Song first made lavish burial, using clam charcoal and adding chariots and horses; his ministers Hua Yuan and Yue Ju were recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals as disloyal ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Duke Wen of Song first made lavish burial, using clam charcoal and adding chariots and horses; his ministers Hua Yuan and Yue Ju were recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals as disloyal ministers.

sentences.zh: 秦始皇葬驪山，魚膏為燈燭，水銀為江海，珍寶之藏，不可勝計，千載非之。

translations.literal: The First Emperor of Qin was buried at Mount Li with fish fat for lamps and mercury for rivers and seas; treasures stored were beyond counting, and for a thousand years he has been condemned.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor of Qin was buried at Mount Li with fish fat for lamps and mercury for rivers and seas; treasures stored were beyond counting, and for a thousand years he has been condemned.

sentences.zh: 宋桓魋為石槨，夫子曰：「不如速朽」。

translations.literal: Huan Tui of Song made a stone outer coffin; the Master said, "Better to decay quickly."
translations.idiomatic: Huan Tui of Song made a stone outer coffin; the Master said, "Better to decay quickly."

sentences.zh: 子遊問喪具，夫子曰：「稱家之有無」。

translations.literal: Ziyou asked about funeral equipment; the Master said, "Match what the family has."
translations.idiomatic: Ziyou asked about funeral equipment; the Master said, "Match what the family has."

sentences.zh: 張釋之對孝文曰：「使其中無可欲，雖無石槨，又何戚焉？」

translations.literal: Zhang Shizhi replied to Emperor Xiaowen, "If inside there is nothing desirable, though there be no stone outer coffin, what sorrow is there?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shizhi replied to Emperor Xiaowen, "If inside there is nothing desirable, though there be no stone outer coffin, what sorrow is there?"

sentences.zh: 漢文帝霸陵皆以瓦器，不以金銀為飾。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han's Baling tomb all used earthenware and did not use gold or silver as ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han's Baling tomb all used earthenware and did not use gold or silver as ornament.

sentences.zh: 由是觀之，有德者葬逾薄，無德者葬逾厚，昭然可睹矣！

translations.literal: From this it is seen that the burial of the virtuous grows ever more modest and that of the unvirtuous grows ever more lavish— plainly visible!
translations.idiomatic: From this it is seen that the burial of the virtuous grows ever more modest and that of the unvirtuous grows ever more lavish— plainly visible!

sentences.zh: 陛下自臨禦天下，聖政日新。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty personally governs the realm, sacred governance grows daily new.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty personally governs the realm, sacred governance grows daily new.

sentences.zh: 進忠去邪，減膳節用，不珍雲物之瑞，不近鷹犬之娛。

translations.literal: You advance the loyal and remove the corrupt, reduce meals and economize expense, do not prize auspicious clouds and objects, and do not draw near to hawk and hound amusements.
translations.idiomatic: You advance the loyal and remove the corrupt, reduce meals and economize expense, do not prize auspicious clouds and objects, and do not draw near to hawk and hound amusements.

sentences.zh: 有司給物，悉依元估，利於人也。

translations.literal: When offices supply goods, all follow original estimates— benefiting the people.
translations.idiomatic: When offices supply goods, all follow original estimates— benefiting the people.

sentences.zh: 遠方底貢，唯供祀事，薄於己也。

translations.literal: Tribute from distant regions supplies only sacrificial affairs— sparing yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute from distant regions supplies only sacrificial affairs— sparing yourself.

sentences.zh: 故澤州奏慶雲，詔曰：「以時和為嘉祥」；

translations.literal: Therefore when Ze Prefecture reported auspicious clouds, the edict said, "Take timely harmony as auspicious omen;"
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when Ze Prefecture reported auspicious clouds, the edict said, "Take timely harmony as auspicious omen;"

sentences.zh: 邕州奏金坑，詔曰：「以不貪為寶」。

translations.literal: when Yong Prefecture reported a gold mine, the edict said, "Take not being greedy as treasure."
translations.idiomatic: when Yong Prefecture reported a gold mine, the edict said, "Take not being greedy as treasure."

sentences.zh: 恭惟聖慮，無非至理。

translations.literal: Respectfully considering the sacred mind, nothing is not ultimate principle.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully considering the sacred mind, nothing is not ultimate principle.

sentences.zh: 而獨六月一日制節文雲「應緣山陵制度，務從優厚，當竭帑藏，以供費用」者，此誠仁孝之德，切於聖衷。

translations.literal: Yet alone in the regulation text of the first day of the sixth month it says, "Because of the tomb system, strive for generous treatment and exhaust the treasury to supply expense"— this is truly virtue of benevolence and filial piety, pressing on the sacred heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yet alone in the regulation text of the first day of the sixth month it says, "Because of the tomb system, strive for generous treatment and exhaust the treasury to supply expense"— this is truly virtue of benevolence and filial piety, pressing on the sacred heart.

sentences.zh: 伏以尊親之義，貴於合禮。

translations.literal: I respectfully consider that the meaning of honoring parents values conforming to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully consider that the meaning of honoring parents values conforming to ritual.

sentences.zh: 陛下每下明詔，發德音，皆比蹤唐、虞，超邁周、漢。

translations.literal: Whenever Your Majesty issues bright edicts and sends forth virtuous words, you always trace Tang and Yu and surpass Zhou and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Your Majesty issues bright edicts and sends forth virtuous words, you always trace Tang and Yu and surpass Zhou and Han.

sentences.zh: 豈取悅凡常之目，有違賢哲之心，與失德之君競其奢侈者也？

translations.literal: Would you please common eyes and go against the mind of sages and worthies, competing in extravagance with rulers who lost virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Would you please common eyes and go against the mind of sages and worthies, competing in extravagance with rulers who lost virtue?

sentences.zh: 臣又伏讀遺詔曰：「其喪儀制度，務從儉約，不得以金銀錦彩為飾。」

translations.literal: Your subject also respectfully read the testamentary edict: "Its funeral rites and system should strive for frugality and not use gold, silver, brocade, or colored silk as ornament."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject also respectfully read the testamentary edict: "Its funeral rites and system should strive for frugality and not use gold, silver, brocade, or colored silk as ornament."

sentences.zh: 陛下恭順先誌，動無違者。

translations.literal: Your Majesty respectfully follows the prior will and in action never violates it.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty respectfully follows the prior will and in action never violates it.

sentences.zh: 若制度優厚，豈顧命之意耶？

translations.literal: If the system is generous, how is that the meaning of the dying command?
translations.idiomatic: If the system is generous, how is that the meaning of the dying command?

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下遠覽虞、夏、周、漢之制，深惟夫子、張釋之之誡，虔奉先旨，俯遵禮經，為萬代法，天下幸甚！

translations.literal: I respectfully ask Your Majesty to look far to the systems of Yu, Xia, Zhou, and Han, deeply weigh the warnings of the Master and Zhang Shizhi, reverently follow the prior intent, defer to the ritual classics, and make a law for ten thousand generations— great fortune for the realm!
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully ask Your Majesty to look far to the systems of Yu, Xia, Zhou, and Han, deeply weigh the warnings of the Master and Zhang Shizhi, reverently follow the prior intent, defer to the ritual classics, and make a law for ten thousand generations— great fortune for the realm!

sentences.zh: 今赦書雖已頒行，諸條尚猶未出，此時奉遺制，敷聖理，固未晚也。

translations.literal: Though the amnesty edict has already been promulgated, the various articles have not yet come out; at this time to follow the testamentary system and spread sacred principle is still not late.
translations.idiomatic: Though the amnesty edict has already been promulgated, the various articles have not yet come out; at this time to follow the testamentary system and spread sacred principle is still not late.

sentences.zh: 伏望速詔有司，悉從古禮。

translations.literal: I respectfully hope you will quickly order the responsible offices to follow entirely the ancient rites.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully hope you will quickly order the responsible offices to follow entirely the ancient rites.

sentences.zh: 臣聞愚夫之言，明主擇焉。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the words of foolish men are chosen by a bright ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard that the words of foolish men are chosen by a bright ruler.

sentences.zh: 況臣忝職史官，親逢睿德，恥同華元、樂舉之為不臣也，願以舜、禹之理，紀聖猷也。

translations.literal: Moreover your subject disgracefully holds the post of historiographer and personally met enlightened virtue; ashamed to be like Hua Yuan and Yue Ju in disloyalty, I wish to record the principle of Shun and Yu in the sacred plan.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover your subject disgracefully holds the post of historiographer and personally met enlightened virtue; ashamed to be like Hua Yuan and Yue Ju in disloyalty, I wish to record the principle of Shun and Yu in the sacred plan.

sentences.zh: 夙夜懇迫，不敢不言，抵犯聖明，實憂罪譴。

translations.literal: Day and night in urgent pleading I dare not fail to speak; offending the sacred brightness, I truly fear punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night in urgent pleading I dare not fail to speak; offending the sacred brightness, I truly fear punishment.

sentences.zh: 言行身黜，雖死猶生。

translations.literal: If words are heeded though the person is dismissed, though one dies one still lives.
translations.idiomatic: If words are heeded though the person is dismissed, though one dies one still lives.

sentences.zh: 優詔答曰：「朕頃議山陵，心方迷謬，忘遵先旨，遂有優厚之文。

translations.literal: A gracious reply answered, "I recently deliberated on the imperial tomb and my mind was confused and mistaken; forgetting to follow the prior intent, there came the generous text.
translations.idiomatic: A gracious reply answered, "I recently deliberated on the imperial tomb and my mind was confused and mistaken; forgetting to follow the prior intent, there came the generous text.

sentences.zh: 卿聞見該通，識度弘遠，深知不可，形於至言。

translations.literal: You are comprehensive in knowledge and far-reaching in judgment, deeply knowing it cannot be done, and expressed it in utmost words.
translations.idiomatic: You are comprehensive in knowledge and far-reaching in judgment, deeply knowing it cannot be done, and expressed it in utmost words.

sentences.zh: 援引古今，依據經禮，非唯中朕之病，抑亦成朕之躬。

translations.literal: Citing past and present and relying on the classics and rites, you not only hit my fault but also completed my person.
translations.idiomatic: Citing past and present and relying on the classics and rites, you not only hit my fault but also completed my person.

sentences.zh: 免朕獲不子之名，皆卿之力也。

translations.literal: Spared me the name of an unfilial son— all your power.
translations.idiomatic: Spared me the name of an unfilial son— all your power.

sentences.zh: 敢不聞義而徙，收之桑榆，奉以始終，期無失墜。

translations.literal: How dare I not hear righteousness and move, gather it at sunset, and follow it to the end, expecting no lapse!
translations.idiomatic: How dare I not hear righteousness and move, gather it at sunset, and follow it to the end, expecting no lapse!

sentences.zh: 古之遺直，何以加焉！」

translations.literal: How can the upright men of antiquity be surpassed!"
translations.idiomatic: How can the upright men of antiquity be surpassed!"

sentences.zh: 初，大歷中，劉晏為吏部尚書，楊炎為侍郎，晏用峘判吏部南曹事。

translations.literal: Formerly in the Dali era Liu Yan was Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Yang Yan was Vice Director; Yan used Huhuan to judge southern bureau affairs in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly in the Dali era Liu Yan was Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Yang Yan was Vice Director; Yan used Huhuan to judge southern bureau affairs in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 峘荷晏之舉，每分闕，必擇其善者送晏，不善者送炎，炎心不平之。

translations.literal: Huhuan, obliged by Yan's recommendation, whenever dividing vacancies always sent the good ones to Liu Yan and the poor ones to Yang Yan; Yang Yan was displeased in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Huhuan, obliged by Liu Yan's recommendation, whenever dividing vacancies always sent the best candidates to Liu Yan and the weaker ones to Yang Yan; Yang Yan was displeased.

sentences.zh: 及建中初，亙為禮部侍郎，炎為宰相，不念舊事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era Gen was Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and Yan was chancellor; he did not remember old affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era Gen was Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and Yan was chancellor; he did not remember old affairs.

sentences.zh: 有士子杜封者，故相鴻漸子，求補弘文生。

translations.literal: There was a scholar named Du Feng, son of the former chancellor Hongjian, who sought appointment as a student of the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: There was a scholar named Du Feng, son of the former chancellor Hongjian, who sought appointment as a student of the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 炎嘗出杜氏門下，托封於峘。

translations.literal: Yan had once been a client of the Du house and entrusted Feng to Huhuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had once been a client of the Du house and entrusted Feng to Huhuan.

sentences.zh: 峘謂使者曰：「相公誠憐封，欲成一名，乞署封名下一字，峘得以誌之。」

translations.literal: Huhuan said to the messenger, "If the chancellor truly pities Feng and wishes to make a name for him, please sign one character below Feng's name so Huhuan may record it."
translations.idiomatic: Huhuan said to the messenger, "If the chancellor truly pities Feng and wishes to make a name for him, please sign one character below Feng's name so Huhuan may record it."

sentences.zh: 炎不意峘賣，即署名托封。

translations.literal: Yan did not expect Huhuan's trick and at once signed, entrusting Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Yan did not expect Huhuan's trick and at once signed, entrusting Feng.

sentences.zh: 峘以炎所署奏論，言宰相迫臣以私，臣若從之，則負陛下，不從則炎當害臣。

translations.literal: Huhuan submitted a memorial with Yan's signature, saying the chancellor forced your subject for private reasons; if your subject followed, then he failed Your Majesty; if he did not follow, Yan would harm your subject.
translations.idiomatic: Huhuan submitted a memorial with Yan's signature, saying the chancellor forced your subject for private reasons; if your subject followed, then he failed Your Majesty; if he did not follow, Yan would harm your subject.

sentences.zh: 德宗出疏問炎，炎具言其事，德宗怒甚，曰：「此奸人，無可奈何！」

translations.literal: Dezong issued the memorial to question Yan; Yan fully explained the matter, and Dezong was greatly angry and said, "This is a treacherous man— nothing can be done!"
translations.idiomatic: Dezong issued the memorial to question Yan; Yan fully explained the matter, and Dezong was greatly angry and said, "This is a treacherous man— nothing can be done!"

sentences.zh: 欲決杖流之，炎苦救解，貶衡州別駕。

translations.literal: He wished to have him beaten with the rod and banished; Yan bitterly pleaded for mercy and Huhuan was demoted Assistant Administrator of Heng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to have him beaten with the rod and banished; Yan bitterly pleaded for mercy and Huhuan was demoted Assistant Administrator of Heng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遷衡州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Prefect of Heng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Prefect of Heng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，李泌輔政，召拜右庶子、史館修撰。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era Li Mi assisted in governance and summoned him as Right Subordinate and Historiography Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenyuan era Li Mi assisted in governance and summoned him as Right Subordinate and Historiography Compiler.

sentences.zh: 性既僻異，動失人和。

translations.literal: By nature he was eccentric and often failed in human harmony.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was eccentric and often failed in human harmony.

sentences.zh: 在史館，與同職孔述睿等爭忿細故，數侵述睿。

translations.literal: In the Historiography Office he quarreled over small matters with colleagues such as Kong Shurui and repeatedly offended Shurui.
translations.idiomatic: In the Historiography Office he quarreled over small matters with colleagues such as Kong Shurui and repeatedly offended Shurui.

sentences.zh: 述睿長者，讓而不爭。

translations.literal: Shurui was a man of forbearance and yielded without quarreling.
translations.idiomatic: Shurui was a man of forbearance and yielded without quarreling.

sentences.zh: 無何，泌卒，竇參秉政，惡其為人，貶吉州別駕。

translations.literal: Before long Mi died and Dou Can held power; he hated Huhuan's conduct and demoted him Assistant Administrator of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Mi died and Dou Can held power; he hated Huhuan's conduct and demoted him Assistant Administrator of Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 久之，授吉州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed Prefect of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was appointed Prefect of Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 齊映廉察江西，行部過吉州。

translations.literal: Qi Ying inspected Jiangxi and on tour passed through Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Ying inspected Jiangxi and on tour passed through Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 故事，刺史始見觀察使，皆戎服趨庭致禮；

translations.literal: By precedent, when a prefect first met an observation commissioner he all wore military dress and hastened to the court to perform ritual;
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when a prefect first met an observation commissioner he all wore military dress and hastened to the court to perform ritual;

sentences.zh: 映雖嘗為宰相，然驟達後進，峘自恃前輩，有以過映，不欲以戎服謁。

translations.literal: though Ying had once been chancellor, he had suddenly risen as a later arrival; Huhuan relied on being a senior and looked down on Ying and did not wish to meet in military dress.
translations.idiomatic: though Ying had once been chancellor, he had suddenly risen as a later arrival; Huhuan relied on being a senior and looked down on Ying and did not wish to meet in military dress.

sentences.zh: 入告其妻韋氏，恥抹首趨庭。

translations.literal: He told his wife Lady Wei and was ashamed to smear his head and hasten to court.
translations.idiomatic: He told his wife Lady Wei and was ashamed to smear his head and hasten to court.

sentences.zh: 謂峘曰：「卿自視何如人，白頭走小生前，卿如不以此禮見映，雖黜死，我亦無恨。」

translations.literal: He said to Huhuan, "What sort of man do you take yourself for— white-haired, running before a junior? If you do not meet Ying with this rite, though demoted to death, I have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: He said to Huhuan, "What sort of man do you take yourself for— white-haired, running before a junior? If you do not meet Ying with this rite, though demoted to death, I have no regret."

sentences.zh: 峘曰「諾」，即以客禮謁之。

translations.literal: Huhuan said, "Agreed," and met him with guest rites.
translations.idiomatic: Huhuan said, "Agreed," and met him with guest rites.

sentences.zh: 映雖不言，深以為憾。

translations.literal: Though Ying did not speak of it, he deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Though Ying did not speak of it, he deeply resented it.

sentences.zh: 映至州，奏峘糾前政過失，鞫之無狀，不宜按部臨人，貶衢州別駕。

translations.literal: When Ying reached the prefecture he memorialized that Huhuan had investigated faults of the prior administration; investigation found no basis, and he was unsuitable to inspect the region and govern people; Huhuan was demoted Assistant Administrator of Qu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying reached the prefecture he memorialized that Huhuan had investigated faults of the prior administration; investigation found no basis, and he was unsuitable to inspect the region and govern people; Huhuan was demoted Assistant Administrator of Qu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 衢州刺史田敦，峘知舉時進士門生也。

translations.literal: Prefect Tian Dun of Qu Prefecture was a jinshi disciple when Huhuan supervised the examination.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Tian Dun of Qu Prefecture was a jinshi disciple when Huhuan supervised the examination.

sentences.zh: 初峘當貢部，放榜日貶逐，與敦不相面。

translations.literal: When Huhuan first supervised the Ministry of Rites, on the day the list was posted he was demoted and banished and never met Dun face to face.
translations.idiomatic: When Huhuan first supervised the Ministry of Rites, on the day the list was posted he was demoted and banished and never met Dun face to face.

sentences.zh: 敦聞峘來，喜曰：「始見座主。」

translations.literal: When Dun heard Huhuan was coming he rejoiced and said, "At last I see my examiner."
translations.idiomatic: When Dun heard Huhuan was coming he rejoiced and said, "At last I see my examiner."

sentences.zh: 迎謁之禮甚厚。

translations.literal: The welcoming and audience rites were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: The welcoming and audience rites were very generous.

sentences.zh: 敦月分俸之半以奉峘。

translations.literal: Each month Dun gave half his salary to support Huhuan.
translations.idiomatic: Each month Dun gave half his salary to support Huhuan.

sentences.zh: 峘在衢州殆十年。

translations.literal: Huhuan was in Qu Prefecture for nearly ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Huhuan was in Qu Prefecture for nearly ten years.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，以秘書少監征，既至而卒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shunzong ascended the throne he was summoned as Vice Director of the Secretariat; once he arrived he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong ascended the throne he was summoned as Vice Director of the Secretariat; once he arrived he died.

sentences.zh: 元和三年，峘子太仆寺丞丕，始獻峘所撰《代宗實錄》四十卷。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanhe Huhuan's son Pi, Assistant Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, first presented the Veritable Record of Emperor Daizong in forty juan that Huhuan had compiled.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanhe Huhuan's son Pi, Assistant Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, first presented the Veritable Record of Emperor Daizong in forty juan that Huhuan had compiled.

sentences.zh: 初，亙坐李泌貶，監修國史奏峘所撰實錄一分，請於貶所畢功。

translations.literal: Formerly Gen was demoted because of Li Mi; the supervising compiler of the national history memorialized one copy of the Veritable Record Huhuan had compiled and asked that he finish the work at his place of demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Gen was demoted because of Li Mi; the supervising compiler of the national history memorialized one copy of the Veritable Record Huhuan had compiled and asked that he finish the work at his place of demotion.

sentences.zh: 至是方奏，以功贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: Only then was it submitted; for the achievement he was posthumously granted Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Only then was it submitted; for the achievement he was posthumously granted Director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 歸崇敬

translations.literal: Gui Chongjing
translations.idiomatic: Gui Chongjing

sentences.zh: 歸崇敬，字正禮，蘇州吳郡人也。

translations.literal: Gui Chongjing, styled Zhengli, was a native of Wu Commandery in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Chongjing, styled Zhengli, came from Wu Commandery in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖奧，以崇敬故，追贈秘書監。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Ao, because of Chongjing, was posthumously granted Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Ao, because of Chongjing, was posthumously granted Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 祖樂，贈房州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Le was posthumously granted Prefect of Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Le was posthumously granted Prefect of Fang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父待聘，亦贈秘書監。

translations.literal: His father Daipin was also posthumously granted Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daipin was also posthumously granted Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 崇敬少勤學，以經業擢第。

translations.literal: Chongjing from youth studied diligently and was selected by classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjing from youth studied diligently and was selected by classical learning.

sentences.zh: 遭喪哀毀，以孝聞，調授四門助教。

translations.literal: When he encountered mourning he was destroyed in grief and was famed for filial piety; he was appointed Assistant Instructor of the Four Gates.
translations.idiomatic: When he encountered mourning he was destroyed in grief and was famed for filial piety; he was appointed Assistant Instructor of the Four Gates.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，對策高第，授左拾遺，改秘書郎。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era, he ranked at the top in the policy-response examination, was appointed Left Reminder, and was changed to Secretary Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Tianbao era, he placed at the top of the policy-response examination, was appointed Left Reminder, and was reassigned as Secretary Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 遷起居郎、贊善大夫，兼史館修撰，又加集賢殿校理。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Diarist and Mentor to the Heir Apparent, concurrently History Office compiler, and additionally appointed collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Diarist and Mentor to the Heir Apparent, served concurrently as a History Office compiler, and was also made collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 以家貧求為外職，歷同州、潤州長史，會玄宗、肅宗二帝山陵，參掌禮儀，遷主客員外郎。

translations.literal: Because his family was poor he sought an outside post, served successively as chief administrator of Tong and Run Prefectures, and when the imperial tombs were built for Emperors Xuanzong and Suzong he took part in managing ritual; he was promoted to Assistant Director of the Bureau of Receiving Guests.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking an outside appointment because his family was poor, he served successively as chief administrator of Tong and Run Prefectures; when the tombs of Emperors Xuanzong and Suzong were prepared, he helped manage the rites, and was promoted to Assistant Director of the Bureau of Receiving Guests.

sentences.zh: 又兼史館修撰，改膳部郎中。

translations.literal: Again concurrently History Office compiler, changed to Director of the Bureau of Food and Drink.
translations.idiomatic: He again served concurrently as a History Office compiler and was reassigned as Director of the Bureau of Food and Drink.

sentences.zh: 崇敬以百官朔望朝服褲褶非古，上疏云：「按三代典禮，兩漢史籍，並無褲褶之制，亦未詳所起之由。

translations.literal: Gui Chongjing held that officials wearing trousers and short jackets at the new- and full-moon court audiences was not ancient custom, and submitted a memorial, "According to the canonical rites of the Three Dynasties and the historical records of the two Han, there is no institution of trousers and short jackets, nor is it clear when it arose.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Chongjing argued that having officials wear trousers and short jackets at the new- and full-moon court audiences was not ancient practice, and submitted a memorial, "Examining the canonical rites of the Three Dynasties and the historical records of the two Han, one finds no institution of trousers and short jackets, nor any clear account of when it began.

sentences.zh: 隋代已來，始有服者。

translations.literal: Since the Sui dynasty, people have begun to wear them.
translations.idiomatic: Only since the Sui dynasty have people begun to wear them.

sentences.zh: 事不師古，伏請停罷。」

translations.literal: Since this does not follow antiquity, I humbly request that it be discontinued."
translations.idiomatic: Because this does not follow antiquity, I humbly ask that it be abolished."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 又諫：「東都太廟，不合置木主。

translations.literal: He also remonstrated, "The Eastern Capital Ancestral Temple should not have wooden spirit tablets installed.
translations.idiomatic: He also remonstrated, "The Eastern Capital Ancestral Temple ought not to keep wooden spirit tablets.

sentences.zh: 謹按典禮，虞主用桑，練主用栗。

translations.literal: According to canonical ritual, the mourning tablet uses mulberry wood, and the refined tablet uses chestnut wood.
translations.idiomatic: According to canonical ritual, the mourning tablet is made of mulberry, and the refined tablet of chestnut.

sentences.zh: 作桑主則埋栗主，作栗主則埋桑主，所以神無二主，天無二日，土無二王也。

translations.literal: When a mulberry tablet is made, the chestnut tablet is buried; when a chestnut tablet is made, the mulberry tablet is buried—thus the spirit has no two masters, Heaven has no two suns, and the land has no two kings.
translations.idiomatic: When a mulberry tablet is made, the chestnut tablet is buried; when a chestnut tablet is made, the mulberry tablet is buried—so that the spirit has no two masters, Heaven no two suns, and the land no two kings.

sentences.zh: 東都太廟，是則天皇后所建，以置武氏木主。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital Ancestral Temple was built by Empress Wu to house the wooden tablets of the Wu clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital Ancestral Temple was built by Empress Wu to install wooden tablets for the Wu clan.

sentences.zh: 中宗去其主而存其廟，蓋將以備行幸遷都之置也。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong removed her tablets but kept the temple, intending it as a reserve for imperial tours and relocation of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong removed her tablets but preserved the temple, evidently to keep a reserve for imperial tours and possible relocation of the capital.

sentences.zh: 且殷人屢遷，前八後五，則前後遷都一十三度，不可每都而別立神主也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Yin people moved their capital repeatedly—eight times before and five after—thirteen relocations in all; one cannot establish separate spirit tablets at every capital.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Yin moved their capital repeatedly—eight times before and five after, thirteen relocations in all—so one cannot set up separate spirit tablets at every capital.

sentences.zh: 議者或云：『東都神主已曾虔奉而禮之，豈可一朝廢之乎？』

translations.literal: Some in the debate object, 'The Eastern Capital spirit tablets were once reverently honored in ritual—how can they be abolished in a single morning?'
translations.idiomatic: Some object, 'The Eastern Capital spirit tablets were once reverently served in ritual—how can they be cast aside overnight?'

sentences.zh: 且虞祭則立桑主而虔祀，練祭則立栗主而埋桑主，豈桑主不曾虔祀而乃埋之？

translations.literal: Yet at the yu sacrifice a mulberry tablet is erected and reverently worshipped, and at the lian sacrifice a chestnut tablet is erected and the mulberry tablet buried—was the mulberry tablet never reverently worshipped, and only then buried?
translations.idiomatic: Yet at the yu sacrifice a mulberry tablet is erected and reverently worshipped, and at the lian sacrifice a chestnut tablet is erected while the mulberry tablet is buried—surely the mulberry tablet was reverently worshipped before it was buried?

sentences.zh: 又所闕之主，何須更作？

translations.literal: As for the missing tablets, why must new ones be made?
translations.idiomatic: And for the tablets that are lacking, why must new ones be made at all?

sentences.zh: 作之不時，恐非禮也。」

translations.literal: To make them out of season would, I fear, be unritual."
translations.idiomatic: To make them at the wrong time, I fear, would not be ritual."

sentences.zh: 又議云：「每年春秋二時釋奠文宣王，祝板禦署訖，北面揖，臣以為禮太重。

translations.literal: He also submitted an opinion, "Each spring and autumn, when the sacrifice to Confucius is performed, after the prayer board is signed by the emperor the officiant bows facing north; I consider this ritual excessively heavy.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted an opinion, "In the spring and autumn sacrifices to Confucius, after the prayer board is signed by the emperor the officiant bows facing north; I consider this excessively solemn.

sentences.zh: 謹按《大戴禮》，師尚父授周武王丹書，武王東面而立。

translations.literal: According to the Greater Dai Book of Rites, Military Instructor Shangfu presented King Wu with the Red Book, and Wu stood facing east.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Greater Dai Book of Rites, Military Instructor Shangfu presented King Wu with the Red Book, and Wu stood facing east.

sentences.zh: 今署祝板，伏請準武王東面之禮，輕重庶得其中。」

translations.literal: Now, when the prayer board is signed, I humbly request that Wu's east-facing rite be taken as the standard, so that the weight of the ceremony may be properly balanced."
translations.idiomatic: When the prayer board is signed today, I humbly ask that the east-facing rite of King Wu be taken as the standard, so that the ceremony's weight may be properly balanced."

sentences.zh: 時有術士巨彭祖上疏云：「大唐土德，千年合符，請每四季郊祀天地。」

translations.literal: At that time the adept Ju Pengzu submitted a memorial, "The Great Tang possesses the virtue of Earth; the thousand-year tally is fulfilled—please sacrifice to Heaven and Earth in all four seasons."
translations.idiomatic: At that time the adept Ju Pengzu submitted a memorial, "The Great Tang possesses the virtue of Earth and the thousand-year tally is fulfilled—I ask that Heaven and Earth be sacrificed to in all four seasons."

sentences.zh: 詔禮官儒者議之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered ritual officials and Confucian scholars to debate it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered ritual officials and Confucian scholars to discuss the proposal.

sentences.zh: 崇敬議曰：「按舊禮，立春之日，迎春於東郊，祭青帝。

translations.literal: Gui Chongjing submitted an opinion, "According to the old rites, on the day of the Beginning of Spring one welcomes spring at the eastern suburb and sacrifices to the Green Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Chongjing submitted an opinion, "According to the old rites, on the day of Beginning of Spring one welcomes spring at the eastern suburb and sacrifices to the Green Emperor.

sentences.zh: 立夏之日，迎夏於南郊，祭赤帝。

translations.literal: On the day of the Beginning of Summer one welcomes summer at the southern suburb and sacrifices to the Red Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of Beginning of Summer one welcomes summer at the southern suburb and sacrifices to the Red Emperor.

sentences.zh: 先立秋十八日，迎黃靈於中地，祀黃帝。

translations.literal: Eighteen days before the Beginning of Autumn one welcomes the Yellow Spirit at the central region and sacrifices to the Yellow Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen days before Beginning of Autumn one welcomes the Yellow Spirit at the central region and sacrifices to the Yellow Emperor.

sentences.zh: 秋、冬各於其方。

translations.literal: Autumn and winter each have their respective directions.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn and winter each have their own directional rites.

sentences.zh: 黃帝於五行為土王，在四季生於火，故火用事之末而祭之，三季則否。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor, as sovereign of Earth among the Five Phases, is born at the end of the season of Fire; therefore he is sacrificed at the close of Fire's dominion, but not in the other three seasons.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor, as sovereign of Earth among the Five Phases, arises at the end of Fire's season; therefore he is sacrificed at the close of Fire's dominion, but not in the other three seasons.

sentences.zh: 漢、魏、周、隋，共行此禮。

translations.literal: Han, Wei, Zhou, and Sui all followed this rite.
translations.idiomatic: Han, Wei, Zhou, and Sui all followed this rite.

sentences.zh: 國家土德乘時，亦以每歲六月土王之日，祀黃帝於南郊，以後土配，所謂合禮。

translations.literal: Our state, riding the fortune of the virtue of Earth, also each year on the day of the Earth sovereign in the sixth month sacrifices to the Yellow Emperor at the southern suburb, with Hou Tu as associate—this is what is called conformity to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Our state, inheriting the virtue of Earth, likewise each year on the day of the Earth sovereign in the sixth month sacrifices to the Yellow Emperor at the southern suburb with Hou Tu as associate—this is true conformity to ritual.

sentences.zh: 今彭祖請用四季祠祀，多憑緯候之說，且據陰陽之說。

translations.literal: Now Pengzu asks to use seasonal sacrifices in all four quarters, relying heavily on apocryphal prognostications and on yin-yang theory.
translations.idiomatic: Now Pengzu asks to sacrifice in all four seasons, relying heavily on apocryphal prognostications and yin-yang theory.

sentences.zh: 事涉不經，恐難行用。」

translations.literal: The matter is uncanonical, and I fear it would be hard to implement."
translations.idiomatic: The proposal is uncanonical, and I fear it would be difficult to carry out."

sentences.zh: 又議祭五人帝不稱臣云：「太昊五帝，人帝也，於國家即為前後之禮，無君臣之義。

translations.literal: He also debated sacrificing to the Five Human Sovereigns without calling oneself their subject, "Taihao and the Five Sovereigns are human sovereigns; toward the state they are only predecessors in ritual sequence, not a relationship of ruler and subject.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued against calling oneself subject when sacrificing to the Five Human Sovereigns, "Taihao and the Five Sovereigns are human sovereigns; toward the state they are only predecessors in ritual sequence, not rulers in a relationship of subject and sovereign.

sentences.zh: 若於人帝而稱臣，則於天帝復何稱也？

translations.literal: If one calls oneself subject to human sovereigns, then what title does one use toward the Sovereign of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: If one calls oneself subject to human sovereigns, then what title does one use before the Sovereign of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 議者或云：『五人帝列於《月令》，分配五時。』

translations.literal: Some in the debate object, 'The Five Human Sovereigns are listed in the Monthly Ordinances, assigned to the five seasons.'
translations.idiomatic: Some object, 'The Five Human Sovereigns are listed in the Monthly Ordinances and assigned to the five seasons.'

sentences.zh: 則五神、五音、五祀、五蟲、五臭、五谷皆備，以備其時之色數，非謂別有尊崇也。」

translations.literal: Then the five spirits, five tones, five sacrifices, five creatures, five odors, and five grains are all complete, to supply the colors and numbers of each season—not to mean that they receive separate exalted worship."
translations.idiomatic: In that case the five spirits, five tones, five sacrifices, five creatures, five odors, and five grains are all complete, supplying the colors and numbers of each season—not meaning that they receive separate exalted worship."

sentences.zh: 又請太祖景皇帝配天，事已具《禮儀志》。

translations.literal: He also requested that the Founding Emperor Jing be associated with Heaven; the matter is fully recorded in the Treatise on Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested that Founding Emperor Jing be associated with Heaven; the matter is fully recorded in the Treatise on Ritual.

sentences.zh: 自是國典大禮，崇敬常參議焉。

translations.literal: From this time on, in the great rites of state canon, Gui Chongjing regularly took part in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, in the great rites of state, Gui Chongjing regularly took part in deliberation.

sentences.zh: 大歷初，以新羅王卒，授崇敬倉部郎中、兼御史中丞，賜紫金魚袋，充吊祭、冊立新羅使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dali era, when the king of Silla died, Gui Chongjing was appointed Director of the Bureau of Granaries and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, granted the purple robe and gold fish tally, and sent as envoy to mourn, invest, and install the new king of Silla.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Dali era, when the king of Silla died, Gui Chongjing was appointed Director of the Bureau of Granaries and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, granted the purple robe and gold fish tally, and dispatched as envoy to mourn, invest, and install the new king of Silla.

sentences.zh: 至海中流，波濤迅急，舟船壞漏，眾鹹驚駭。

translations.literal: When they reached mid-ocean, the waves surged violently, the ship was damaged and leaking, and all were terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Midway across the sea the waves surged violently, the ship was damaged and leaking, and everyone was terrified.

sentences.zh: 舟人請以小艇載崇敬避禍，崇敬曰：「舟中凡數十百人，我何獨濟？」

translations.literal: The boatmen asked to carry Gui Chongjing away in a small boat to escape disaster. Gui Chongjing said, "There are several dozen or hundred people in this vessel—how can I alone be saved?"
translations.idiomatic: The boatmen asked to carry Gui Chongjing off in a small boat to escape disaster. Gui Chongjing said, "There are several dozen or a hundred people in this vessel—how can I alone be saved?"

sentences.zh: 逡巡，波濤稍息，竟免為害。

translations.literal: Before long the waves gradually subsided, and they ultimately escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the waves gradually subsided, and they ultimately escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 故事，使新羅者，至海東多有所求，或攜資帛而往，貿易貨物，規以為利。

translations.literal: By precedent, envoys to Silla, upon reaching the eastern sea, often made many demands; some carried silks and goods to trade for profit.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, envoys to Silla often made many demands once they reached the eastern sea; some carried silks and goods to trade for profit.

sentences.zh: 崇敬一皆絕之，東夷稱重其德。

translations.literal: Gui Chongjing refused all of this entirely, and the eastern barbarians greatly respected his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Chongjing refused all of this, and the eastern barbarians greatly respected his integrity.

sentences.zh: 使還，授國子司業，兼集賢學士。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Education and Concurrent Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Education and Concurrent Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 與諸儒官同修《通志》，崇敬知《禮儀志》，眾稱允當。
