translations.idiomatic: Where there is excess, suppress it; where there is deficiency, support it—neither diminishing the weak nor seizing from the presumptuous.

sentences.zh: 握中持平，不振不傾，使其求不可得，而蓋不可掩，斯古君子所以慎其名也。

translations.literal: Holding the center level, neither stirring nor tilting, so that what is sought cannot be obtained yet what is covered cannot be hidden—this is how the ancient gentleman was careful with names.
translations.idiomatic: Holding the center level, neither stirring nor tilting, so that what is sought cannot be obtained yet what is covered cannot be hidden—this is how the ancient gentleman was careful with names.

sentences.zh: 夫則天體自坤順，位居乾極，以柔乘剛，天紀倒張，進以強有，退非德讓。

translations.literal: Empress Wu by nature followed Kun's yielding yet occupied Qian's summit, using softness to overcome hardness; heaven's order was overturned, advancing by forcible possession and retreating without virtuous yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu by nature followed Kun's yielding yet occupied Qian's summit, using softness to overcome hardness; heaven's order was overturned, advancing by forcible possession and retreating without virtuous yielding.

sentences.zh: 今史臣追書，當稱之太后，不宜曰「上」。

translations.literal: Now when historiographers write in retrospect they should call her Empress Dowager and should not say "Sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: Now when historiographers write in retrospect they should call her Empress Dowager and should not say "Sovereign."

sentences.zh: 孝和雖迫母後之命，降居籓邸，而體元繼代，本吾君也，史臣追書，宜稱曰「皇帝」，不宜曰「廬陵王」。

translations.literal: Though Xiaozong was compelled by his mother's command and demoted to a princely residence, he embodied the origin and succeeded to the age—he is fundamentally our sovereign; historiographers writing in retrospect should call him "Emperor" and should not say "Prince of Luling."
translations.idiomatic: Though Xiaozong was compelled by his mother's command and demoted to a princely residence, he embodied the origin and succeeded to the age—he is fundamentally our sovereign; historiographers writing in retrospect should call him "Emperor" and should not say "Prince of Luling."

sentences.zh: 睿宗在景龍已前，天命未集，徒稟後制，假臨大寶，於倫非次，於義無名，史臣書之，宜曰「相王」，未宜曰「帝」。

translations.literal: Before Jinglong Ruizong's mandate was not yet gathered; he merely received the empress dowager's command and temporarily held the great treasure—out of order in human relations and without name in righteousness; historiographers writing of him should say "Prince Regent" and should not yet say "Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Before Jinglong Ruizong's mandate was not yet gathered; he merely received the empress dowager's command and temporarily held the great treasure—out of order in human relations and without name in righteousness; historiographers writing of him should say "Prince Regent" and should not yet say "Emperor."

sentences.zh: 若以得失既往，遂而不舉，則是非褒貶，安所辨正，載筆執簡，謂之何哉？

translations.literal: If because gain and loss are already past one lets it pass and does not raise it, then how are right and wrong, praise and blame, to be distinguished and corrected—what does it mean to hold the brush and keep the record?
translations.idiomatic: If because gain and loss are already past one lets it pass and does not raise it, then how are right and wrong, praise and blame, to be distinguished and corrected—what does it mean to hold the brush and keep the record?

sentences.zh: 則天廢國家歷數，用周正朔，廢國家太廟，立周七廟。

translations.literal: Empress Wu abolished the state's dynastic succession, adopted Zhou's calendar, abolished the state's Imperial Ancestral Temple, and established Zhou's seven temples.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu abolished the state's dynastic succession, adopted Zhou's calendar, abolished the state's Imperial Ancestral Temple, and established Zhou's seven temples.

sentences.zh: 鼎命革矣，徽號易矣，旂裳服色，既已殊矣！

translations.literal: The mandate of the tripod was changed, imperial titles were altered, banners, robes, and colors of dress were already different!
translations.idiomatic: The mandate of the tripod was changed, imperial titles were altered, banners, robes, and colors of dress were already different!

sentences.zh: 今安得以周氏年歷而列為《唐書》帝紀？

translations.literal: How can one now use Zhou's yearly chronology and list it as an imperial annal in the Book of Tang?
translations.idiomatic: How can one now use Zhou's yearly chronology and list it as an imperial annal in the Book of Tang?

sentences.zh: 征諸禮經，是謂亂名。

translations.literal: Consulting the ritual classics, this is called disordering names.
translations.idiomatic: Consulting the ritual classics, this is called disordering names.

sentences.zh: 且孝和繼天踐祚，在太后之前，而敘年制紀，居太后之下；

translations.literal: Moreover Xiaozong succeeded to heaven and took the throne before the empress dowager, yet in arranging years and fixing annals he is placed below the empress dowager;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Xiaozong succeeded to heaven and took the throne before the empress dowager, yet in arranging years and fixing annals he is placed below the empress dowager;

sentences.zh: 方之躋僖。

translations.literal: compared to elevating Duke Xi, this is called unwise.
translations.idiomatic: compared to elevating Duke Xi, this is called unwise.

sentences.zh: 是謂不智，詳今考古，並未為可。

translations.literal: Examining the present against antiquity, none of it is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the present against antiquity, none of it is acceptable.

sentences.zh: 或曰：班、馬良史也，編述漢事，立高後以續帝載，豈有非之者乎？

translations.literal: Some say: Ban and Sima were fine historians; in compiling Han affairs they established Empress Gao to continue the imperial record—was there anyone who objected?
translations.idiomatic: Some say: Ban and Sima were fine historians; in compiling Han affairs they established Empress Gao to continue the imperial record—was there anyone who objected?

sentences.zh: 答曰：昔高後稱制，因其曠嗣，獨有分王諸呂，負於漢約，無遷鼎革命之甚。

translations.literal: The reply: In former times Empress Gao held sole rule because the heir's line was vacant; she alone enfeoffed the various Lüs, betraying Han's covenant—there was nothing so grave as shifting the tripod and transforming the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The reply: In former times Empress Gao held sole rule because the heir's line was vacant; she alone enfeoffed the various Lüs, betraying Han's covenant—there was nothing so grave as shifting the tripod and transforming the mandate.

sentences.zh: 況其時孝惠已歿，孝文在下，宮中二子，非劉氏種，不紀呂後，將紀誰焉？

translations.literal: Moreover at that time Emperor Xiaohui was already dead and Emperor Xiaowen was below; the two sons in the palace were not of the Liu clan—if Empress Lü were not recorded, whom would one record?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover at that time Emperor Xiaohui was already dead and Emperor Xiaowen was below; the two sons in the palace were not of the Liu clan—if Empress Lü were not recorded, whom would one record?

sentences.zh: 雖雲其然，議者猶為不可，況遷鼎革命者乎？

translations.literal: Though one may say it was so, debaters still held it impermissible—how much more when the tripod is shifted and the mandate transformed?
translations.idiomatic: Though one may say it was so, debaters still held it impermissible—how much more when the tripod is shifted and the mandate transformed?

sentences.zh: 或曰：若天後不紀，帝緒缺矣，則二十二年行事，何所系乎？

translations.literal: Some say: If the empress dowager is not recorded, the imperial line is broken—then to what are twenty-two years of actions attached?
translations.idiomatic: Some say: If the empress dowager is not recorded, the imperial line is broken—then to what are twenty-two years of actions attached?

sentences.zh: 曰：孝和以始年登大位，以季年復舊業，雖尊名中奪，而天命未改，足以首事，足以表年，何所拘閡，裂為二紀？

translations.literal: The answer: Xiaozong at the first year ascended the great throne and at the last year restored the former enterprise; though his honored name was seized in the middle, the mandate of heaven was not changed—sufficient to head affairs and sufficient to mark the year; what constraint requires splitting it into two annals?
translations.idiomatic: The answer: Xiaozong at the first year ascended the great throne and at the last year restored the former enterprise; though his honored name was seized in the middle, the mandate of heaven was not changed—sufficient to head affairs and sufficient to mark the year; what constraint requires splitting it into two annals?

sentences.zh: 昔魯昭之出也，《春秋》歲書其居，曰「公在乾侯」。

translations.literal: In former times when Duke Zhao of Lu went into exile, the Spring and Autumn Annals each year recorded where he was, saying "The Duke was at Ganhou."
translations.idiomatic: In former times when Duke Zhao of Lu went into exile, the Spring and Autumn Annals each year recorded where he was, saying, "The Duke was at Ganhou."

sentences.zh: 且君在，雖失位，不敢廢也。

translations.literal: Moreover while the ruler lives, though he loses position, he is not abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover while the ruler lives, though he loses position, he is not abolished.

sentences.zh: 今請並《天後紀》合《孝和紀》，每於歲首，必書孝和所在以統之，書曰某年春正月，皇帝在房陵，太后行某事，改某制云云。

translations.literal: I now request merging the Empress Dowager Annal with the Xiaozong Annal; at the head of each year one must record where Xiaozong was to unify it, writing: In such-and-such year, spring, first month, the emperor was at Fangling; the empress dowager performed such-and-such affair and changed such-and-such regulation, and so on.
translations.idiomatic: I now request merging the Empress Dowager Annal with the Xiaozong Annal; at the head of each year one must record where Xiaozong was to unify it, writing: In such-and-such year, spring, first month, the emperor was at Fangling; the empress dowager performed such-and-such affair and changed such-and-such regulation, and so on.

sentences.zh: 則紀稱孝和，而事述太后，俾名不失正，而禮不違常；

translations.literal: Then the annal would be titled Xiaozong while affairs would narrate the empress dowager, so that the name would not lose rectitude and ritual would not violate the constant;
translations.idiomatic: Then the annal would be titled Xiaozong while affairs would narrate the empress dowager, so that the name would not lose rectitude and ritual would not violate the constant;

sentences.zh: 名禮兩得，人無間矣！

translations.literal: name and ritual both obtained, and no one would find fault!
translations.idiomatic: name and ritual both obtained, and no one would find fault!

sentences.zh: 其姓氏名諱，入宮之由，歷位之資，才藝智略，年辰崩葬，別纂錄入《皇后傳》，列於廢後王庶人之下，題其篇曰「則天順聖武後」云。

translations.literal: Her surname, personal name, taboo, the reason for entering the palace, qualifications for successive offices, talent, wisdom, and stratagem, year of birth, death, and burial should be separately compiled into the Biography of the Empress, placed below the deposed empress and commoner consorts, with the chapter title "Empress Zetian Shunsheng Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Her surname, personal name, taboo, the reason for entering the palace, qualifications for successive offices, talent, wisdom, and stratagem, year of birth, death, and burial should be separately compiled into the Biography of the Empress, placed below the deposed empress and commoner consorts, with the chapter title "Empress Zetian Shunsheng Wu."

sentences.zh: 事雖不行，而史氏稱之。

translations.literal: Though the proposal was not adopted, historians praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Though the proposal was not adopted, historians praised it.

sentences.zh: 德宗初即位，銳於求理。

translations.literal: When Dezong first ascended the throne he was keen to seek good governance.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong first ascended the throne he was keen to seek good governance.

sentences.zh: 建中二年夏，敕中書、門下兩省，分置待詔官三十員，以見官前任及同正試攝九品已上，擇文學理道、韜鈐法度之深者為之，各準品秩給俸錢，廩餼、幹力、什器、館宇之設，以公錢為之本，收息以贍用。

translations.literal: In summer of the second year of Jianzhong an edict ordered the Secretariat and Chancellery to each establish thirty awaiting-edict posts, drawn from former officials of rank nine and above in regular, probationary, and acting status who were skilled in letters, principles, military arts, and law—each receiving salary according to rank, with pantry provisions, laborers, utensils, and lodging established from public funds as capital, collecting interest to support expenses.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of the second year of Jianzhong an edict ordered the Secretariat and Chancellery to each establish thirty awaiting-edict posts, drawn from former officials of rank nine and above in regular, probationary, and acting status who were skilled in letters, principles, military arts, and law—each receiving salary according to rank, with pantry provisions, laborers, utensils, and lodging established from public funds as capital, collecting interest to support expenses.

sentences.zh: 物論以為兩省皆名侍臣，足備顧問，無勞別置冗員。

translations.literal: Public opinion held that both bureaus already had attendant ministers sufficient for consultation and there was no need separately to establish superfluous posts.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion held that both bureaus already had attendant ministers sufficient for consultation and there was no need separately to establish superfluous posts.

sentences.zh: 既濟上疏論之曰：

translations.literal: Ji Ji submitted a memorial arguing:
translations.idiomatic: Ji Ji submitted a memorial arguing:

sentences.zh: 臣伏以陛下今日之理，患在官煩，不患員少；

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully observes that in Your Majesty's governance today the worry is that offices are too numerous, not that posts are too few;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject respectfully observes that in Your Majesty's governance today the worry is that offices are too numerous, not that posts are too few;

sentences.zh: 患在不問，不患無人。

translations.literal: the worry is that inquiry is not made, not that there are no men.
translations.idiomatic: the worry is that inquiry is not made, not that there are no men.

sentences.zh: 且中書、門下兩省常侍、諫議、補闕、拾遺，總四十員，及常參待制之官，日有兩人，皆備顧問，亦不少矣。

translations.literal: Moreover the Secretariat and Chancellery together have forty regular attendants, remonstrance and reviser, and remonstrance and reviser posts, and two officials on regular court attendance each day—all sufficient for consultation and not few.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Secretariat and Chancellery together have forty regular attendants, remonstrance and reviser, and remonstrance and reviser posts, and two officials on regular court attendance each day—all sufficient for consultation and not few.

sentences.zh: 中有二十一員，尚闕人未充，他司缺職，累倍其數。

translations.literal: Among them twenty-one posts still lack men to fill them; other offices lack incumbents by many times that number.
translations.idiomatic: Among them twenty-one posts still lack men to fill them; other offices lack incumbents by many times that number.

sentences.zh: 陛下若謂見官非才，不足與議，則當選求能者，以代其人。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty thinks the current officials lack talent and are unfit for deliberation, then capable men should be sought to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty thinks the current officials lack talent and are unfit for deliberation, then capable men should be sought to replace them.

sentences.zh: 若欲務廣聰明，畢收淹滯，則當擇其可者，先補缺員。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty wishes to extend intelligence widely and gather all the overlooked, then among those fit the vacancies should first be filled.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty wishes to extend intelligence widely and gather all the overlooked, then among those fit the vacancies should first be filled.

sentences.zh: 則朝無曠官，俸不徒費。

translations.literal: Then the court would have no vacant offices and salaries would not be wasted.
translations.idiomatic: Then the court would have no vacant offices and salaries would not be wasted.

sentences.zh: 且夫置錢息利，是有司權宜，非陛下經理之法。

translations.literal: Moreover establishing capital to collect interest is an expedient of the relevant offices, not Your Majesty's method of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover establishing capital to collect interest is an expedient of the relevant offices, not Your Majesty's method of governance.

sentences.zh: 今官三十員，皆給俸錢，幹力及廚廩什器、建造廳宇，約計一月不減百萬，以他司息例準之，當以錢二千萬為之本，方獲百萬之利。

translations.literal: Now thirty posts all receive salaries, laborers, and pantry provisions, utensils, and construction of halls—estimated for one month not less than one million cash; measured against interest rates in other offices, capital of twenty million cash would be required to obtain one million in profit.
translations.idiomatic: Now thirty posts all receive salaries, laborers, and pantry provisions, utensils, and construction of halls—estimated for one month not less than one million cash; measured against interest rates in other offices, capital of twenty million cash would be required to obtain one million in profit.

sentences.zh: 若均本配人，當復除二百戶，或許其入流。

translations.literal: If the capital were distributed per person, two hundred households would again have to be exempted, or they might be permitted entry into the official stream.
translations.idiomatic: If the capital were distributed per person, two hundred households would again have to be exempted, or they might be permitted entry into the official stream.

sentences.zh: 反覆計之，所損滋甚。

translations.literal: Reckoned back and forth, the harm grows ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Reckoned back and forth, the harm grows ever greater.

sentences.zh: 當今關輔大病，皆為百司息錢，傷人破產，積於府縣。

translations.literal: Today the great illness of the capital region is that every office lends money at interest, injuring people and ruining households, accumulating in prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Today the great illness of the capital region is that every office lends money at interest, injuring people and ruining households, accumulating in prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 實思改革，以正本源。

translations.literal: I truly wish for reform to rectify the root source.
translations.idiomatic: I truly wish for reform to rectify the root source.

sentences.zh: 又臣嘗計天下財賦耗篸之大者，唯二事焉：最多者兵資，次多者官俸。

translations.literal: Moreover your subject once calculated the greatest drains on the empire's revenue and expenditure: of two matters, the most is military supplies, the next is official salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover your subject once calculated the greatest drains on the empire's revenue and expenditure: of two matters, the most is military supplies, the next is official salaries.

sentences.zh: 其餘雜費，十不當二事之一。

translations.literal: All other miscellaneous expenses do not equal one of these two.
translations.idiomatic: All other miscellaneous expenses do not equal one of these two.

sentences.zh: 所以黎人重困，杼軸猶空。

translations.literal: Therefore the common people are heavily afflicted and the loom is still empty.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the common people are heavily afflicted and the loom is still empty.

sentences.zh: 方期緝熙，必藉裁減。

translations.literal: When one expects order and brilliance, one must rely on cutting and reducing.
translations.idiomatic: When one expects order and brilliance, one must rely on cutting and reducing.

sentences.zh: 今四方形勢，兵罷未得，資費之廣，蓋非獲已。

translations.literal: Now in the four directions the military situation has not yet ceased and expenses are broad—this is surely unavoidable.
translations.idiomatic: Now in the four directions the military situation has not yet ceased and expenses are broad—this is surely unavoidable.

sentences.zh: 陛下躬行儉約，節用愛人，豈俾閑官，復為冗食？

translations.literal: Your Majesty personally practices frugality, economizes expenditure, and cherishes the people—how can idle offices again become superfluous eaters?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty personally practices frugality, economizes expenditure, and cherishes the people—how can idle offices again become superfluous eaters?

sentences.zh: 籍舊而置，猶可省也，若之何加焉？

translations.literal: To establish them from the old registers could still be reduced—how then add more?
translations.idiomatic: To establish them from the old registers could still be reduced—how then add more?

sentences.zh: 陛下必以制出不可改，請重難慎擇，遷延寢罷。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty must hold that the regulation once issued cannot be changed, I request weighing the difficulty carefully, choosing with care, and deferring until it is abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty must hold that the regulation once issued cannot be changed, I request weighing the difficulty carefully, choosing with care, and deferring until it is abandoned.

sentences.zh: 其事竟不得行。

translations.literal: The matter in the end was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The matter in the end was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 既而楊炎譴逐，既濟坐貶處州司戶。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Yang Yan was punished and banished; Ji Ji was implicated and demoted to Registrar of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yang Yan was punished and banished; Ji Ji was implicated and demoted to Registrar of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 後復入朝，位終禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: Later he reentered court and ended as External Official in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Later he reentered court and ended as External Official in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 傳師擢進士，登制科乙第，授太子校書郎、鄠縣尉，直史館，轉左拾遺、左補闕，並兼史職。

translations.literal: Chuanshi passed the jinshi examination and ranked in the second class of the decree examination; he was appointed Proofreader of the Crown Prince and aide of E County, direct appointment to the Historiography Institute, transferred to Left Remonstrance and Reviser and Left Reviser—all concurrently historiographical posts.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanshi passed the jinshi examination and ranked in the second class of the decree examination; he was appointed Proofreader of the Crown Prince and aide of E County, direct appointment to the Historiography Institute, transferred to Left Remonstrance and Reviser and Left Reviser—all concurrently historiographical posts.

sentences.zh: 遷司門員外郎、知制誥，召充翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to External Official in the Ministry of Justice and charged with drafting imperial documents, and was summoned to serve as Academician of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to External Official in the Ministry of Justice and charged with drafting imperial documents, and was summoned to serve as Academician of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 歷司勛、兵部郎中，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: He served successively as Director in the Ministries of Merit and War and was promoted to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Director in the Ministries of Merit and War and was promoted to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 性恬退無競，時翰林未有承旨，次當傳師為之，固稱疾，宣召不起，乞以本官兼史職。

translations.literal: By nature retiring and without contention, at that time the Hanlin Academy had no chief drafter and Chuanshi was next in line; he firmly pleaded illness, would not rise when summoned by imperial order, and begged to hold his current office concurrently with historiographical duty.
translations.idiomatic: By nature retiring and without contention, at that time the Hanlin Academy had no chief drafter and Chuanshi was next in line; he firmly pleaded illness, would not rise when summoned by imperial order, and begged to hold his current office concurrently with historiographical duty.

sentences.zh: 俄兼御史中丞，出為潭州刺史、湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: Soon he was concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief and sent out as prefect of Tan and circuit supervisor of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief and sent out as prefect of Tan and circuit supervisor of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 入為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He entered court as Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 出為洪州刺史、江南西道觀察使，轉宣州刺史、宣歙池觀察使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefect of Hong and circuit supervisor of Jiangxi, transferred to prefect of Xuan and circuit supervisor of Xuan, She, and Chi.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Hong and circuit supervisor of Jiangxi, transferred to prefect of Xuan and circuit supervisor of Xuan, She, and Chi.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered court as Vice Minister of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Vice Minister of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 太和元年卒，年五十九，贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taihe he died, aged fifty-nine; posthumously honored as Minister of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taihe he died, aged fifty-nine; posthumously honored as Minister of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 初，傳師父既濟撰《建中實錄》十卷，為時所稱。

translations.literal: Initially Chuanshi's father Ji Ji compiled the Jianzhong Veritable Record in ten scrolls, praised at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Chuanshi's father Ji Ji compiled the Jianzhong Veritable Record in ten scrolls, praised at the time.

sentences.zh: 傳師在史館，預修《憲宗實錄》未成，廉察湖南，特詔賫一分史稿，成於理所。

translations.literal: While Chuanshi was in the Historiography Institute he participated in compiling the Xianzong Veritable Record, which was unfinished; when he was made supervisory commissioner of Hunan, a special edict sent him one portion of the historiographical draft, and he completed it in his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: While Chuanshi was in the Historiography Institute he participated in compiling the Xianzong Veritable Record, which was unfinished; when he was made supervisory commissioner of Hunan, a special edict sent him one portion of the historiographical draft, and he completed it in his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 有子樞、詢，皆登進士第。

translations.literal: He had sons Shu and Xun; both passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He had sons Shu and Xun; both passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 詢歷清顯，中書舍人、翰林學士、禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Xun held clear and eminent posts: Secretariat Drafter, Academician of the Hanlin Academy, and Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Xun held clear and eminent posts: Secretariat Drafter, Academician of the Hanlin Academy, and Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，檢校戶部尚書、潞州長史、昭義節度使。

translations.literal: In the Xiantong era he served as acting Minister of Revenue, Chief Administrator of Lu Prefecture, and military commissioner of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiantong era he served as acting Minister of Revenue, Chief Administrator of Lu Prefecture, and military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 為政簡易，性本恬和。

translations.literal: His governance was simple and easy; by nature he was fundamentally mild and harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: His governance was simple and easy; by nature he was fundamentally mild and harmonious.

sentences.zh: 奴歸秦者，通詢侍者，詢將戮之未果；

translations.literal: A slave named Gui Qin had relations with Xun's attendants; Xun intended to execute him but did not succeed;
translations.idiomatic: A slave named Gui Qin had relations with Xun's attendants; Xun intended to execute him but did not succeed;

sentences.zh: 奴結牙將為亂，夜攻府第，詢舉家遇害。

translations.literal: the slave joined with the garrison officers to raise disorder, attacked the prefectural residence by night, and Xun's entire household was killed.
translations.idiomatic: the slave joined with the garrison officers to raise disorder, attacked the prefectural residence by night, and Xun's entire household was killed.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰

translations.literal: The historiographer comments
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer comments

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：前代以史為學者，率不偶於時，多罹放逐，其故何哉？

translations.literal: The historiographer comments: Scholars who took history as their study in former ages mostly did not meet with fortune in their times and often suffered banishment—why is this?
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer comments: Scholars who took history as their study in former ages mostly did not meet with fortune in their times and often suffered banishment—why is this?

sentences.zh: 誠以褒貶是非在於手，賢愚輕重系乎言，君子道微，俗多忌諱，一言切己，嫉之如仇。

translations.literal: Truly because praise and blame, right and wrong, rest in the hand, and the weight of worthy and unworthy hangs on words—when the gentleman's way is slight and the vulgar are full of taboo, one word that cuts to the self is hated like an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Truly because praise and blame, right and wrong, rest in the hand, and the weight of worthy and unworthy hangs on words—when the gentleman's way is slight and the vulgar are full of taboo, one word that cuts to the self is hated like an enemy.

sentences.zh: 所以峘、薦坎壈於仕塗，沈、柳不登於顯貫，後之載筆執簡者，可以為之痛心！

translations.literal: Therefore Han and Zhang suffered hardship on the official road, and Shen and Liu did not reach eminent rank—later men who hold the brush and keep the record may grieve for them!
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Han and Zhang suffered hardship on the official road, and Shen and Liu did not reach eminent rank—later men who hold the brush and keep the record may grieve for them!

sentences.zh: 道在必伸，物不終否，子孫藉其餘祐，多至公卿者，蓋有天道存焉！

translations.literal: The Way must extend; things do not end in denial—their descendants relied on their remaining blessing and many reached the rank of chief minister; surely the Way of Heaven is preserved therein!
translations.idiomatic: The Way must extend; things do not end in denial—their descendants relied on their remaining blessing and many reached the rank of chief minister; surely the Way of Heaven is preserved therein!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：褒貶以言，孔道是模。

translations.literal: In praise it is said: Praise and blame lie in words; the way of Confucius is the model.
translations.idiomatic: In praise it is said: Praise and blame lie in words; the way of Confucius is the model.

sentences.zh: 誅亂以筆，亦有董狐。

translations.literal: To punish disorder with the brush—there is also a Dong Hu.
translations.idiomatic: To punish disorder with the brush—there is also a Dong Hu.

sentences.zh: 邦家大典，班、馬何辜？

translations.literal: The great canon of state and family—what wrong did Ban and Sima commit?
translations.idiomatic: The great canon of state and family—what wrong did Ban and Sima commit?

sentences.zh: 懲惡勸善，史不可無。

translations.literal: To punish evil and encourage good—history cannot be absent.
translations.idiomatic: To punish evil and encourage good—history cannot be absent.
